rows.step: Step 1: Observe panel-edge preparation and hardware presentation
rows.objective: Around 00:00-00:34, recognize the close-up panel-edge work before the wall-assembly sequence.
rows.instruments: Applicator gun; insulated panels; presented metal fasteners; gloves.
rows.actions:
Observe the applicator held over the exposed panel edge and the close-up of metal fasteners in a gloved hand.
Record the visible panel edge and timber-facing detail without deciding that the joint is sealed or fastened correctly.
rows.criteria:
Visual observation: An applicator and exposed insulated panel edge appear together in a close-up.
Visual observation: Metal fasteners are visibly presented in a gloved hand.
Visual observation: A close-up shows the panel or timber edge being joined.

rows.step: Step 2: Observe the ground-floor wall enclosure
rows.objective: Around 00:34-01:05, identify a visible change from the deck and partial wall layout to a more enclosed ground-floor outline.
rows.instruments: Installed deck; wall panels; timber supports; ladders shown in the work area.
rows.actions:
Compare consecutive wide views of the same building area.
Observe workers moving or positioning wall sections and the resulting visible wall outline.
rows.criteria:
Visual observation: Wide views show upright wall panels around the ground-floor deck.
Visual observation: Later views show a more developed wall perimeter than earlier views in this excerpt.
Visual observation: At least one opening or interior partition is visible in the ground-floor enclosure.

rows.step: Step 3: Observe upper-floor framing and the next wall level
rows.objective: Around 01:05-01:35, identify the upper-floor framing and the emerging upper-storey wall outline.
rows.instruments: Timber floor members; installed panels; visible building openings.
rows.actions:
Observe the upper level from the fixed wide camera position.
Compare the exposed upper-floor members with the later upright wall panels.
rows.criteria:
Visual observation: Timber members or decking span the top of the lower wall enclosure.
Visual observation: A later wide view shows upright panels forming the next storey.

rows.step: Step 4: Observe upper-wall edge work and roof-outline growth
rows.objective: Around 01:35-02:06, recognize a close-up of upper-wall edge work followed by the developing roof shape.
rows.instruments: Applicator gun; upper wall panel; timber roof members.
rows.actions:
Observe the close-up applicator work at an upper wall edge.
Compare the following wide views as timber members form a pitched roof outline.
rows.criteria:
Visual observation: The applicator is held along the exposed upper panel edge.
Visual observation: Wide views show pitched roof members above the upper-storey walls.

rows.step: Step 5: Observe roof support and connection details
rows.objective: Around 02:06-02:32, distinguish the exposed roof timber and support details shown in close-ups.
rows.instruments: Roof timbers; support beam; visible metal connection hardware.
rows.actions:
Observe the close-up of roof members meeting a support beam.
Observe the worker and the subsequent close-up of exposed timber joints or support points.
rows.criteria:
Visual observation: Two or more roof members and their support region are visible together.
Visual observation: A close-up exposes a timber connection or bearing region.

rows.step: Step 6: Observe external sheet and roof-covering work
rows.objective: Around 02:32-03:00, identify visible external sheeting and the roof-covering activity near the end of the excerpt.
rows.instruments: Dark external sheet material; roof covering; installed house frame.
rows.actions:
Observe workers presenting or handling a dark sheet beside the building.
Observe the wide exterior frame, the sheet-handling activity, and the close-up roof-covering activity.
rows.criteria:
Visual observation: Dark sheet material is handled or visible on an exterior surface.
Visual observation: A worker and installed roof-covering rows are visible in the roof view.
Visual observation: An exterior view shows the roof and upper wall outline together.

principles: This is real, previously edited construction footage. The original includes time-lapse sequences and close-up inserts; three minutes of playback do not represent three minutes of site work.
Observe visible assembly phases. This guide is an educational viewing aid, not an approved construction method, building inspection, or site instruction.
Source captions identify some materials and dimensions. Treat those as source claims; they do not establish measurements, specifications, suitability, or compliance in the observed building.

Approximate time windows refer to this excerpt, not the original full video. A camera cut, completed-looking surface, or later construction phase does not prove that hidden operations were performed correctly.

Mark a step observed only when its listed visual evidence appears. Keep obscured, missing, or ambiguous details unobserved. Do not infer fastening strength, alignment tolerance, structural capacity, inspection, or approval.
The tools and materials below identify items shown in the footage. They are not a purchasing list or instructions to reproduce hazardous site activity.

Protect people and property. Do not copy work-at-height, access, lifting, or tool-use practices from this film; the responsible site supplies its own safe method, competent supervision, and inspections.
Record the observed phase, location, and any obscured connection separately.

Actual drawings, material grades, dimensions, fastener requirements, access controls, site safety, inspections, and approval require the responsible construction professionals. None are supplied or certified by this footage.
